title: Why the Sky is Blue and Sunsets are Red
subject: Physics
objective: Air scatters blue light far more than red. Blue fills the sky by day; at sunset the long path through the air removes the blue, and red and orange reach you.

fill.q: Scattering by tiny air molecules is called ____ scattering.
____ light scatters about 5-6 times more than red.
On the Moon the sky looks ____ because there is no atmosphere.

tf.q: Red light scatters more than blue light.
At sunset, sunlight travels through more air.
tf.explain: The blue is scattered out on the way.

tf.q: Without an atmosphere the sky would be black.
The sky is blue because it reflects the ocean.
tf.explain: It is due to scattering by air molecules.

ar.r: Air molecules scatter short wavelengths most.

ar.a: Sunsets look red because red light is scattered most.
ar.r: At sunset light travels a long path through air.
ar.explain: A is false (blue is scattered out, red remains); R is true.

mcq.q: The sky appears blue because blue light:

options: blue is scattered out over a long path

mcq.q: Rayleigh scattering depends on wavelength as:
The sky on the Moon is:

num.q: Using scattering ∝ 1/λ⁴, how many times more is blue light (450 nm) scattered than red light (700 nm)?

short.solution: Air molecules scatter sunlight; scattering ∝ 1/λ⁴, so blue (short wavelength) scatters much more and fills the sky.

short.q: Why are sunrises and sunsets red?
short.solution: Near the horizon sunlight crosses much more air; most blue is scattered away, leaving red and orange to reach us.

match.explain: Wavelength and path length decide the sky's colour.
